explain.say: Here is a secret. Scientists, doctors, and astronauts ask for help all the time. Asking is not weak. It is smart! Look at the board. Here is the path when you get stuck.

explain.say: Help comes from people and from helpers. Ask a person: Can you show me? Say it again? I am stuck here. Other helpers: a word mat, a dictionary, an example. Brilliant! Your challenge: ask for help once today.

faq.a: No. Asking for help is how everyone learns, even grown-ups and experts. Cheating is copying answers. Asking is learning.

faq.q: What can I say when I need help?
faq.a: You can say, Can you show me, please? or I am stuck on this part, or What does this word mean?
asks: Tell me about Ask for help
Tell me about Ask a person

faq.a: Look at examples, word mats, pictures, a dictionary or your notes. These are helpers too.
asks: Tell me about Look for clues

faq.a: Trying first shows you what you know and exactly where you are stuck. Then your helper knows how to help.

faq.q: What if I feel embarrassed to ask?
faq.a: Lots of people feel that. You can ask quietly, or write a note. A grown-up you trust is always happy to help.

facts: Astronauts on the International Space Station work closely with teams on the ground who help them.
Asking a question helps you learn exactly the part you are stuck on.

quiz.say: You are stuck. What is a smart thing to say?
quiz.show: You are stuck. What can you say?
quiz.why: Asking to be shown is smart. It helps you learn.

wrong.1: No need to give up. Ask for help instead.
wrong.2: Guessing can lead you the wrong way. Asking helps you learn.
